html:
The Kutubiyya is the largest mosque of Marrakesh, built by the Almohads in the mid-1100s. Its square stone minaret, about 77 metres high, was finished around 1195 and is the landmark of the city.

Abd al-Mumin built a first mosque after taking Marrakesh in 1147, then a second, the one that stands, beside it. The name comes from the booksellers who once gathered at its foot. Its plain, strong decoration set the style of the Almohad age.

The minaret was the model for two others of the same period: the Giralda of Seville in Spain and the unfinished Hassan Tower in Rabat. See also Ibn Tumart and the Hassan II Mosque.
